brief: The wind now reaches the fountain and stops there. The river is the largest surface in the picture and reads the same on a gale as on a still day: `drawRiverFlow()` draws FLOW_N streaks off `riverRun()` alone, `drawRiverLights()` breaks its lamp and moon columns on a fixed chop, and `updateBoat`/`boatRate()` row the same in any weather. Make a windy day legible on the water from the east wide shot — more, shorter, crosswise-slanted streaks and a rougher chop on the reflections when `windF()` is 1, the rowboat rarer and slower into the wind — with every term exact at `windF() = 0` so the calm day and the anchor are byte-identical. Take c78 with it: the rowboat has no reflection after dark and the bridge deck casts no shadow on the water; add both only if they fall out of the same pass.
successLooksLike: A calm-day noon east shot is byte-identical to HEAD; a windy-day shot at the same instant has visibly more and shorter streaks with a lean, and a night windy shot breaks the lamp columns into shorter bars. `river-year.mjs` anchor EXACT; boat presence over ten seeds drops only on windy days.
avoid: Do not touch riverRun()'s seasonal algebra or RIVER_COLD/RIVER_GREEN. No new R() draws in the draw pass — hash() and windT only. Do not make the water read as rain: rainFall already has its sparkle; wind is direction, rain is dots.
